text.p: Digital Equipment Corp. said Thursday it earned $123.9 million in its fourth quarter, reversing a year-ago loss and continuing a string of gains set in motion by its 1996 restructuring.
Digital said growing sales of personal computers and units that connect networks of computers using Microsoft Corp.'s NT software were behind the improvement.

The profit, equal to 75 cents per share, came on revenue of $3.5 billion. In the 1996 period, Digital lost $432.8 million, or $2.87 per share, on revenue of $3.7 billion. The 1996 result included a one-time restructuring charge of $492 million.

Its most recent results were better than the 73 cents a share analysts surveyed by First Call had expected, and Digital's stock jumped $2.125 to $42.125 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
"It was OK, not great," said Steve Milunovich, an analyst at Morgan Stanley. "Revenues are a little light, margins were a little better."
Digital also said it authorised the repurchase of up to 15 million shares of its common stock.
"We achieved improvement for the third straight quarter while further positioning the company for both near-term and long-term," said Robert B. Palmer, chairman.

He said Digital's personal computer business achieved a higher level of profit for the third straight quarter, continuing a significant turnaround from the third quarter of fiscal 1996, when it was hurt by significant price competition and high levels of inventory.
The Windows NT segment grew about 50 percent over the comparable quarter a year earlier, Digital said.
It said its gross margins improved in the fiscal fourth quarter to 34.6 percent of revenues, up from 32.6 percent a year earlier, and were its best in more than three years.
"This reflects continuing improvements in product cost, productivity programmes and mix," said Digital Chief Financial Officer Vincent J. Mullarkey.
Digital said product revenues for the quarter were $2.0 billion, versus $2.1 billion a year ago and up 9 percent from the third quarter.
Service revenues were $1.5 billion, compared with $1.6 billion a year earlier.
For the year, Digital earned $140.9 million, or 68 cents a share, on sales of $13 billion. A year earlier, it lost $111.8 million, or 97 cents a share, on sales of $14.6 billion.
